title: Dynamics of a massive binary at birth
question: Is the massive protostar IRAS07299-1651 a binary at birth, what are its orbital dynamics and masses, and does this support disk fragmentation as the formation mechanism?

evidence.loc: Estimating protostellar masses from free-free emission
evidence.quote: consistent with the $(1-4)\times10^4\:L_\odot$ estimate for the total bolometric luminosity of this system(cite: Debuizer17)

what.value: Dust opacity 0.00899 cm2/g at 1.3 mm incl. gas-to-dust 100

evidence.quote: an opacity of $\kappa_\mathrm{1.3mm}=0.00899~\mathrm{cm}^2~\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ with a standard gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100 included (ref. (cite: Ossenkopf94))

recipe.method: CLEAN imaging with robust 0.5 after self-calibration; source positions with imfit
Gaussian fits to spectra at continuum peaks; uncertainties by Monte Carlo noise and sinusoidal perturbation for asymmetry
assumptions: H30a central velocities trace protostar radial velocities

recipe.goal: Derive orbital constraints and mass ratio
recipe.method: Circular and elliptical orbit limits from apparent separation and velocity difference; mass ratio from center-of-mass velocity
assumptions: Center-of-mass velocity equals cloud systemic velocity 16.5-18 km/s

recipe.goal: Separate free-free and dust continuum and estimate protostar masses
recipe.method: Line-to-continuum ratio under LTE optically thin assumption; ionizing photon rates to ZAMS and protostellar evolution masses

recipe.goal: Fit rotating ring to H30a centroids
recipe.method: Per-channel 2D Gaussian centroids (>20 sigma) fit with half-ring model, chi2 minimisation
key_parameters: weights w_pos=0.9, w_int=0.1; thermal broadening FWHM 19 km/s
assumptions: Keplerian rotation; only half of ring emits

recipe.goal: Model large-scale infall and estimate gas masses
recipe.method: Rotating-infall parabola model to CH3OH PV diagram; optically thin dust mass for extended emission
key_parameters: Tdust 50-100 K, kappa1.3mm=0.00899 cm2/g, D=1680 pc

answer_key.quantity: free-free flux A / B at 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: We estimate free-free components in the 1.3 mm continuum to be 39 mJy and 4 mJy in Sources A and B
corresponding to a central mass of $6\pm2\:M_\odot$
This model requires a central mass of $27\pm6~M_\odot$
the mass of this ambient gas is estimated to be $3.8-8~M_\odot$
